meta.name: Oceania & Antarctica
meta.description: All Australian, New Zealand, Pacific Island, and Antarctic (IceCube, South Pole) STEM & Physics hubs and regional milestones.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

hubs.name: IceCube Neutrino Observatory
hubs.summary: A cubic-kilometer neutrino telescope buried 2 km beneath Antarctic ice, catching ghostly particles from distant black holes.
hubs.nobel: Pioneered high-energy neutrino astronomy across 58 partner universities worldwide.

stages.highschool: IceCube Masterclasses (analyze real South Pole neutrino events with physicists).
stages.undergrad: NSF REU at UW–Madison WIPAC or summer projects at DESY, RWTH Aachen, or Geneva.
stages.masters: MSc thesis inside any of the 58 IceCube member universities (e.g. TU Munich, RWTH Aachen, Uppsala).
stages.phd: PhD in astroparticle physics; opportunity to deploy hardware at the South Pole during Austral summer.
stages.postdoc: WIPAC / DESY / IceCube-Gen2 postdoctoral fellowships leading real-time multimessenger alerts.
stages.assoc_prof: Institution PI leading an IceCube-Gen2 instrumentation or analysis working group.
stages.prof: Collaboration Spokesperson & multi-national NSF/BMBF infrastructure leadership.

hubs.name: UNSW Sydney Quantum
hubs.summary: World leader in single-atom silicon spin qubits, building quantum processors out of the same silicon that runs modern chips.
hubs.nobel: Leads Australia's CQC2T with world-record silicon spin-qubit coherence.

stages.highschool: Australian Science Olympiads & UNSW Quantum Engineering outreach.
stages.undergrad: UNSW Taste of Research summer scholarships in silicon quantum computing.
stages.masters: English MPhil / Master of Physics with Australian Government RTP full scholarships.
stages.phd: Funded 3.5-year PhD inside CQC2T & Silicon Quantum Computing.
stages.assoc_prof: ARC Future Fellowship & UNSW Associate Professor.

projects.name: ARC Centre of Excellence for Quantum Computation (CQC2T)

hubs.name: Q-CTRL
hubs.summary: University of Sydney spinout applying quantum control engineering to suppress decoherence in quantum processors and build GPS-free cold-atom quantum navigation sensors.

stages.highschool: Explore Black Opal interactive visual lessons on qubits, Bloch spheres, and quantum control physics.
stages.undergrad: Summer internships in Sydney, Los Angeles, and Berlin in quantum control software, cold atoms, and DSP.
stages.masters: Graduate engineering & physics internships in optimal control, error suppression, and quantum sensing hardware.
stages.phd: PhD research internships & Quantum Control Scientist tracks in pulse engineering and cold-atom gravimetry/navigation.
stages.postdoc: Lead Quantum Physicist roles for AMO, quantum-sensing, and open-quantum-systems postdocs.
stages.assoc_prof: Academic Boulder Opal licenses, joint University of Sydney / ARC quantum-control grants, and co-publications.
stages.prof: Strategic defense/civilian quantum-navigation consortia and co-supervised industrial PhD programs.

hubs.name: Quantum Brilliance
hubs.summary: Australian National University spinout building room-temperature diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center quantum accelerators requiring no cryogenics or vacuum chambers.

stages.highschool: Discover how room-temperature diamond NV-center defects act as solid-state spins without liquid helium.
stages.undergrad: Summer internships in Canberra and Stuttgart in diamond nanophotonics, microwave control, and Qristal SDK.
stages.masters: MSc/MEng projects in precision ion implantation, optical confocal detection, and edge quantum-accelerator software.
stages.phd: PhD internships & Research Scientist tracks in NV-center spin coherence, diamond nanofabrication, and hybrid HPC.
stages.postdoc: Senior Quantum Physicist roles for solid-state spin, diamond NV-center, and quantum-sensing postdocs.
stages.assoc_prof: Joint ANU / Fraunhofer IAF / Pawsey Supercomputing Centre collaborations on room-temperature quantum clusters.
stages.prof: Australian ARC & German BMBF collaborative grants co-developing diamond fabrication and edge QPU ecosystems.

hubs.name: ARC Centre for Quantum Computation & Communication Technology (CQC2T)
hubs.summary: Australia's flagship multi-university quantum computing consortium headquartered in Sydney, world-leading in atomic-precision silicon spin qubits, optical quantum networks, and quantum software verification.
hubs.nobel: Led by Michelle Simmons (2018 Australian of the Year), pioneering single-atom phosphorus-in-silicon transistors and integrated quantum processors.

projects.name: Atomic-Scale Silicon Quantum Processors & Optical Networks

hubs.name: Garvan Institute of Medical Research
hubs.summary: Australia's flagship genomics and precision-medicine institute in Sydney's Darlinghurst precinct—driving population whole-genome sequencing, single-cell cellular genomics, and rare-disease and cancer diagnostics.

hubs.name: Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research (WEHI)
hubs.summary: Australia's oldest medical research institute in Melbourne's Parkville biomedical precinct—pioneer of adaptive immunology, colony-stimulating factors (Donald Metcalf), structural virology, and BCL-2 apoptosis therapeutics (venetoclax).
hubs.nobel: Former director Sir Frank Macfarlane Burnet won the 1960 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for acquired immunological tolerance.

hubs.name: Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)
hubs.summary: Australia's tropical marine research agency at Cape Ferguson—operating the National Sea Simulator (SeaSim) and research fleet to decode Great Barrier Reef coral genetics, heat-tolerant symbiont evolution, and reef restoration.

projects.name: Long-Term Great Barrier Reef Monitoring Program

hubs.name: Australian Antarctic Division (AAD)
hubs.summary: Australia's polar science agency in Hobart operating the icebreaker RSV Nuyina and four Antarctic and sub-Antarctic stations—leading East Antarctic ice-sheet mass-balance surveys, Southern Ocean ecosystems, and the Million Year Ice Core.

projects.name: Million Year Ice Core & East Antarctic Glaciology

hubs.name: GNS Science (Te Pū Ao)
hubs.summary: New Zealand's national geoscience and isotope institute sitting astride the Pacific–Australian plate boundary—operating the GeoNet real-time earthquake, volcano, and tsunami network and studying Hikurangi slow-slip subduction quakes.

projects.name: GeoNet Real-Time Seismic, Tsunami & Volcano Network

hubs.name: UNSW Sydney Photovoltaics & Renewable Energy Engineering (SPREE)
hubs.summary: Home to Martin Green's world-famous silicon photovoltaics group, inventors of the PERC (Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell) solar cell architecture that powers over 80% of solar panels manufactured globally today.
hubs.nobel: Martin Green and UNSW colleagues won the 2023 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering for inventing PERC solar cell technology.

projects.name: PERC, TOPCon & Silicon-Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells

hubs.name: CSIRO Manufacturing (Clayton Hub)
hubs.summary: Australia's national industrial materials and advanced-manufacturing campus in Clayton, pioneering Lab 22 titanium 3D-printed biomedical implants, supersonic cold-spray metal additive manufacturing, and RAFT living polymer synthesis.
hubs.nobel: CSIRO chemists invented RAFT (Reversible Addition-Fragmentation chain-Transfer) polymerization—a foundational tool of modern precision polymer materials.

projects.name: Lab 22 Metal Additive Manufacturing & Titanium Medical Implants
Supersonic Cold-Spray Metallurgy & Precision RAFT Polymers

hubs.name: Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station
hubs.summary: Elevated year-round US Antarctic Program station at the Geographic South Pole (2,835 m) hosting IceCube, the South Pole Telescope, BICEP/Keck, and NOAA's Clean Air Sector.

hubs.name: South Pole Telescope (SPT)
hubs.summary: 10 m millimeter/submillimeter telescope (SPT-3G) in the South Pole Dark Sector mapping Cosmic Microwave Background polarization, galaxy clusters, dark energy, and EHT black holes.

hubs.name: BICEP / Keck Array CMB Observatory
hubs.summary: Cryogenic refracting CMB polarimeters (Harvard, Caltech, Stanford, UMN) searching the ultra-dry South Pole sky for primordial gravitational-wave B-mode signatures of cosmic inflation.

hubs.name: IceCube-Gen2 (Upcoming South Pole Observatory)
hubs.summary: Next-generation 8 km³ optical & 500 km² radio neutrino observatory at the South Pole expanding IceCube's instrumented ice volume 8× to map PeV–EeV cosmic accelerators.

hubs.name: McMurdo Station & NASA Balloon Facility
hubs.summary: Antarctica's largest research & logistics hub (Crary Science Lab) and launch site for NASA's Long-Duration Stratospheric Balloons (ANITA, PUEO, GUSTO, SPIDER, SuperTIGER) circling the South Pole.

hubs.name: Scott Base (Antarctica New Zealand)
hubs.summary: New Zealand's year-round Antarctic research station founded by Sir Edmund Hillary in 1957, powered by Ross Island wind turbines and supporting Ross Ice Shelf & Dry Valleys science.

hubs.name: Concordia Station (Dome C)
hubs.city: Dome C, East Antarctic Plateau, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Joint French–Italian off-grid interior plateau base (3,233 m, -80°C winter) serving as ESA's spaceflight isolation analog, EPICA 800,000-year ice-core site, and ASTEP exoplanet observatory.

hubs.name: Beyond EPICA — Little Dome C Camp
hubs.summary: Major 12-institute European deep-drilling field camp 34 km from Concordia that reached bedrock at 2,800 m in January 2025, recovering continuous ice spanning over 1.2 million years of Earth's atmospheric and climate history.

hubs.name: Vostok Station & Subglacial Lake Vostok
hubs.summary: Inland plateau station (3,488 m) holding Earth's coldest recorded temperature (-89.2°C), newly modernized in 2024 directly above subglacial Lake Vostok sealed beneath 4 km of ice.

hubs.name: Kunlun Station & AST3 Telescopes (Dome A)
hubs.summary: Highest research station on the Antarctic Plateau (4,093 m) hosting the robotic AST3 wide-field optical survey telescopes at Earth's premier astronomical seeing and terahertz site.

hubs.name: Dome Fuji Station (Oldest Ice Drilling)
hubs.city: Valkyrie Dome, Queen Maud Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Japan's inland 3,810 m ice-dome station (NIPR) that recovered 720,000-year ice cores and is now leading Phase III deep drilling for million-year-old climate ice.

hubs.name: Halley VI Research Station (BAS)
hubs.summary: Iconic ski-mounted, hydraulically relocatable British Antarctic Survey station on the floating Brunt Ice Shelf (where the Ozone Hole was discovered in 1985); relocated 23 km inland in 2017 and operating summer-only with autonomous micro-turbine winter observatories.

hubs.name: Rothera Research Station (BAS)
hubs.summary: British Antarctic Survey's largest Antarctic hub (newly modernized Discovery Building & wharf for RRS Sir David Attenborough) driving Peninsula marine biology, glaciology, and aviation.

hubs.name: Palmer Station (USAP)
hubs.summary: Year-round US Antarctic marine ecology and Long-Term Ecological Research (LTER) station monitoring rapid glacial retreat and Southern Ocean ecosystem change along the Peninsula.

hubs.name: Neumayer-Station III (AWI)
hubs.city: Ekström Ice Shelf, Queen Maud Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Alfred Wegener Institute's hydraulic stilt-mounted off-grid station housing meteorological, atmospheric chemistry, geomagnetic, seismic, infrasound, and PALAOA underwater acoustic observatories.

hubs.name: Princess Elisabeth Antarctica (Zero-Emission Base)
hubs.summary: World's first 100% zero-emission off-grid polar research station (Belgium / IPF) running entirely on wind turbines, solar photovoltaics, smart microgrids, and passive thermal architecture.

hubs.name: Troll Research Station & TrollSat
hubs.summary: Norway's year-round Antarctic station anchored on ice-free bedrock hosting TrollSat polar satellite downlinks, Galileo navigation receivers, and the Troll atmospheric observatory.

hubs.name: Syowa Station & PANSY Radar (Japan)
hubs.city: East Ongul Island, Lützow-Holm Bay, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Japan's flagship year-round Antarctic research station operating the 1,045-antenna PANSY MST atmospheric radar, auroral/geomagnetic arrays, and Dome Fuji inland logistics.

hubs.name: Mawson Research Station (AAD)
hubs.city: Horseshoe Harbour, Mac. Robertson Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Oldest continuously operated research station south of the Antarctic Circle, hosting underground cosmic-ray muon telescopes, geomagnetic observatories, and wind-powered microgrids.

hubs.name: Davis Research Station (AAD)
hubs.city: Vestfold Hills, Princess Elizabeth Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Australia's busiest Antarctic station set in the ice-free Vestfold Hills oasis conducting upper-atmosphere lidar physics, hypersaline lake microbiology, and sea-ice dynamics.

hubs.name: Casey Research Station (AAD)
hubs.summary: Gateway to Wilkins Blue-Ice Aerodrome, Law Dome glaciology, and Australia's Million Year Ice Core (MYIC) inland traverse operations across East Antarctica.

hubs.name: Dumont d'Urville Station (IPEV)
hubs.summary: France's year-round coastal Antarctic base running geomagnetic, lidar, and Emperor penguin ecosystem observatories, and staging heavy 1,100 km overland supply raids to Concordia.

hubs.name: Mario Zucchelli Station (PNRA)
hubs.city: Terra Nova Bay, Victoria Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Italy's primary Ross Sea coastal research station conducting Southern Ocean polynya oceanography, volcanology, marine genomics, and Italian logistics for Concordia Station.

hubs.name: Jang Bogo Antarctic Research Station (KOPRI)
hubs.city: Terra Nova Bay, Victoria Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Korea Polar Research Institute's year-round aerodynamic station investigating Ross Sea ice shelves, space weather, meteorites, and autonomous polar robotics.

hubs.name: Qinling Station (New Ross Sea Base)
hubs.summary: China's newest year-round Antarctic station (opened Feb 2024) featuring hybrid wind-solar renewable microgrids for Ross Sea marine ecology, oceanography, and atmospheric monitoring.

hubs.name: Zhongshan Station
hubs.summary: Year-round Prydz Bay research hub conducting conjugate auroral & ionospheric radar observations (paired with Svalbard's Yellow River Station) and inland traverses to Dome A.

hubs.name: Bharati Research Station (India)
hubs.summary: India's futuristic modular year-round station (NCPOR) housing the AGEOS polar satellite ground station, oceanographic labs, and continental-breakup geological studies.

hubs.name: Maitri Research Station (India)
hubs.city: Schirmacher Oasis, Queen Maud Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: India's permanent Schirmacher Oasis station (with next-generation Maitri II planned) studying East Antarctic geology, glaciology, geomagnetism, and polar medicine.

hubs.name: SANAE IV (South African National Antarctic Base)
hubs.city: Vesleskarvet Nunatak, Queen Maud Land, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Dramatic cliff-top off-grid research base anchored on an exposed granite nunatak 170 km inland operating SuperDARN space-weather radar, neutron monitors, and auroral physics instruments.

hubs.name: Esperanza Base
hubs.summary: Year-round Argentine research station on the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula conducting glaciology, seismology, meteorology, and long-term Peninsula warming records.

hubs.name: Marambio Base
hubs.summary: Primary all-season Antarctic Peninsula aviation hub and atmospheric ozone, cosmic-ray, paleontology, and greenhouse-gas monitoring observatory.

hubs.name: Comandante Ferraz Antarctic Station (Rebuilt 2020)
hubs.city: King George Island, South Shetland Islands, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Brazil's award-winning rebuilt (2020) 4,500 m² research complex housing 17 laboratories for Antarctic atmospheric physics, marine microbiology, and polar oceanography.

hubs.name: Carlini Station & Dallmann Laboratory
hubs.city: Potter Cove, King George Island, Antarctica
hubs.summary: Argentine–German coastal marine biology and glacial-retreat observatory tracking newly ice-free fjord colonization and Southern Ocean acidification.

hubs.name: Vernadsky Research Base (fmr. Faraday)
hubs.summary: Ukraine's year-round Peninsula station maintaining one of Antarctica's longest unbroken climate, ozone, ionospheric, and geomagnetic records since 1947.

hubs.name: International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration (ITGC)
hubs.summary: Major US–UK off-grid deep-field research campaign deploying hot-water drills, autonomous underwater robots (Icefin), and icebreakers to forecast sea-level rise from Thwaites Glacier.

hubs.name: Scott's Terra Nova Hut — Cape Evans (Historic)
hubs.summary: Remarkably preserved 1911 Heroic Age scientific base, meteorology station, and darkroom built by Robert Falcon Scott's Terra Nova Expedition on Ross Island.

hubs.name: Mawson's Huts — Cape Denison (Historic)
hubs.summary: Sir Douglas Mawson's 1911–1914 Australasian Antarctic Expedition base at Commonwealth Bay—the windiest sea-level location on Earth—pioneering Antarctic radio, geology, and meteorology.

hubs.name: Macquarie Island Research Station (AAD)
hubs.summary: Remote Sub-Antarctic UNESCO World Heritage island station halfway between Australia and Antarctica running seismic, upper-atmosphere, Southern Ocean cloud, and wildlife observatories.

events.title: Discovery of the Antarctic Ozone Hole & Montreal Protocol
events.figure: Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner & Jonathan Shanklin (BAS)
events.summary: British Antarctic Survey atmospheric scientists published decades of Dobson spectrophotometer measurements revealing catastrophic springtime stratospheric ozone depletion caused by human-made CFCs.
events.impact: Triggered the 1987 Montreal Protocol—the most successful international environmental treaty in history—setting the ozone layer on track to recover.

trails.title: Antarctica: South Pole, Ice Cores & Extreme Observatories
trails.tagline: Cross the white continent from Ross Island and South Pole neutrino/CMB arrays to >1.2-million-year Oldest Ice camps and zero-emission bases.

stops.title: McMurdo Station & NASA Balloon Facility
stops.bridge: Antarctica's main science gateway launches giant NASA stratospheric balloons that circle the continent at 38 km altitude hunting ultra-high-energy cosmic rays.

stops.title: Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station (90°S)
stops.bridge: Fly 1,350 km inland to 2,835 m elevation at the Geographic South Pole—the cleanest, driest sky on Earth for millimeter cosmology and neutrino astronomy.

stops.title: South Pole Telescope & BICEP/Keck
stops.bridge: In the radio-quiet Dark Sector, cryogenic telescopes map Cosmic Microwave Background polarization back to the first trillionth of a trillionth of a second after the Big Bang.

stops.title: IceCube & Upcoming IceCube-Gen2
stops.bridge: Deep beneath the polar plateau, optical and upcoming radio arrays turn 8 km³ of ultra-clear glacial ice into humanity's largest particle detector.

stops.title: Concordia Station & Beyond EPICA (Dome C)
stops.bridge: At -80°C winter isolation, Europe's Little Dome C drill reaches 2,800 m bedrock to recover continuous >1.2-million-year-old ancient air bubbles.

stops.title: Vostok Station & Subglacial Lake Vostok
stops.bridge: At Earth's coldest recorded point (-89.2°C), researchers study a vast liquid freshwater lake sealed beneath 4 km of Antarctic ice for 15 million years.

stops.title: Halley VI Research Station (Brunt Ice Shelf)
stops.bridge: Hydraulic ski-mounted modules glide across moving ice shelves where BAS scientists first discovered the Antarctic Ozone Hole in 1985.

stops.title: Princess Elisabeth Antarctica (Zero-Emission)
stops.bridge: Conclude at the world's first 100% wind- and solar-powered off-grid polar research station proving zero-carbon science is possible in Earth's harshest climate.
